anomalies.observed: Both terminals of R61 (10K, TAYLOR_RESISTOR) sit on the same +3V3 net, so the resistor is shorted across itself and connects nothing.
anomalies.expected: A 10K pull-up or series resistor in this position should bridge +3V3 to a distinct signal net, as the other 10K pull-ups (R29, R30, R63, R62) do.
anomalies.impact: The intended pull-up or pull-down function is absent. Whatever signal R61 was meant to bias is left unbiased, so its state floats or depends on the other devices on that line.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of D4, D14 and D23 are the only pins on /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW. No driver or supply pin, such as +3V3 or a switch, reaches that net.
anomalies.expected: LED anodes that are driven through series resistors (R10, R2, R3) need a 3.3V source. The equivalent LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV net is driven by U34.4 and Q10, so the switched-power net should also be connected to a supply.
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet link/activity LEDs (D14, D23) and the Pi activity LED (D4) have no anode supply and cannot light, so the status indication is lost.

anomalies.observed: Q1 (the PMOS of the LTC4412 ideal-diode path) has its source (pin 2) on +5V and its drain (pin 3) on USBC_VBUS_IN. U6.1 VIN is on the USB input and U6.6 SENSE is on +5V.
anomalies.expected: In the LTC4412 power-path arrangement the PMOS source should be on the input supply (VIN, USB VBUS) and its drain on the load (+5V). That way the body diode conducts from the USB input to the rail.

evidence.quote: USBC_VBUS_IN [High Power] : J3.A4(VBUS,passive) ... Q1.3(D,passive) R11.1(passive) R64.2(2,passive) U25.5(VBUS,passive) U6.1(VIN,power_in)

anomalies.impact: If the source and drain are reversed, the PMOS body diode blocks current from USB VBUS to the +5V rail, so USB power may not reach the board. This would match the note that the USB power path does not work.

parsed.summary: The netlist contains a shorted 10K resistor R61 with both pins on +3V3, and LED anodes on /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW that have no supply. Both are concrete deviations from sound practice. The reversed USB PMOS orientation is a lower-confidence concern.
